personas.label: Career changers exploring CRM

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Platform Foundations Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is an easy to moderate exam, but wide. Nothing goes deep, so the work is in covering everything: the data model, the clouds, security, reports, automation and the wider Salesforce ecosystem.
bullets: 62% to pass, about 25 correct answers out of 40. Confirm it in the official exam guide before you book.
Wide but shallow. Expect a little of everything rather than depth in one area.
Wording traps. Several answers in each question sound plausible, so learn the exact names of things.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You are ready when you can say what each standard object is for, tell the clouds apart, and explain in one sentence how profiles, roles and sharing differ. Aim for 80% or more on two full practice tests.

examFormat.heading: Platform Foundations Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About a third of the questions are short scenarios. A typical one describes a business need and asks which object, cloud or feature fits.
bestWayToPass: Learn the standard objects: Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity and Case, and what each one holds.
Tell the clouds apart: Sales Cloud for the pipeline, Service Cloud for support, Marketing Cloud for campaigns, and where Data 360 fits.
Understand the layers of access: Who can log in, which objects and fields they see, and which records.
Know the ecosystem: What AppExchange is for, what Trailhead is, and the difference between a sandbox and production.

expertInsight: This exam is entry level, but the 62% pass mark still catches people out, because the questions are about vocabulary as much as understanding. Several options in each question will sound right. Spend your time learning which standard object holds what, and which cloud does which job, and you will recognise most answers on sight.

certificationCard.description: An entry-level exam for people with a few months of Salesforce experience. It covers the basics: moving around the platform, the standard objects, reports and dashboards, security and where each Salesforce product fits. The exam is 40 scored questions in 70 minutes, with a 62% pass mark, weighted towards Salesforce Ecosystem (32%) and Navigation (28%).

keyConcepts.h2: Salesforce Platform Foundations: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: How the Salesforce Platform Fits Together
blocks.body: Salesforce is a cloud platform shared by many customers, which is called **multi-tenant**: everyone runs on the same infrastructure, with their data kept separate in their own **org**. Because it is shared, Salesforce upgrades everyone three times a year, in the Spring, Summer and Winter releases, and your customisations carry over. The platform is configured mostly through **Setup** rather than code, which is why admins can change a great deal without a developer. **Sandboxes** are copies used for building and testing, so changes are tried out before they reach the live org, which is called **production**.

blocks.heading: The Data Model: Objects, Records and Fields
blocks.body: Salesforce stores data in **objects**, which are like tables. Each row is a **record** and each column a **field**. **Standard objects** come with the platform: a **Lead** is an unqualified prospect, an **Account** is a company, a **Contact** is a person at that company, an **Opportunity** is a potential sale, and a **Case** is a customer issue. **Custom objects** are ones you create for things Salesforce does not cover. Objects are connected by **relationships**: a **lookup** is a loose link, while a **master-detail** link is tighter, with the child record depending on its parent and inheriting its sharing. Converting a Lead turns it into an Account, a Contact and usually an Opportunity.

blocks.heading: Who Can See What
blocks.body: Access is built in layers, and the exam expects you to know the order. First, can the person log in at all, which covers passwords, multi-factor authentication and login hours. Second, which **objects and fields** can they use, which comes from their **profile** and any **permission sets**. Third, which **records** can they see, which starts with the **org-wide default** for each object and is opened up by the **role hierarchy** and **sharing rules**. The simplest way to remember it: profiles and permission sets decide what you can do, while sharing decides which rows you can do it to.

blocks.heading: Automation and Reporting Without Code
blocks.body: **Flow Builder** is the main automation tool. It can update records, send emails and guide users through steps, all without code. **Validation rules** stop bad data being saved. **Approval processes** route a record to someone for sign-off. For reporting, a **report** is a list or summary of records built from a report type, and a **dashboard** shows reports as charts and numbers on one screen. **List views** give a quick filtered list of records on an object's tab. Knowing which tool to reach for is more important here than knowing how to build it.

blocks.heading: The Wider Salesforce Ecosystem
blocks.body: **AppExchange** is the marketplace for ready-made apps and components, some free and some paid, which can be installed into an org. **Trailhead** is Salesforce's free learning site, where modules and trails lead to badges and **Superbadges** for hands-on work. The **Trailblazer Community** is where people ask questions and share solutions. It helps to know the main product families by name, including Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud, Tableau, MuleSoft, Slack and Data 360, and roughly what each is used for.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Platform Foundations Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions ask what something is, or which feature fits a simple need. Precise names matter more than depth here.

blocks.heading: The Core Data Model
blocks.body: Lead, Account, Contact, Opportunity and Case, plus lookup and master-detail relationships. Know what Lead conversion creates.

blocks.heading: Automation Basics
blocks.body: Flow Builder for automation, validation rules to block bad data, approval processes for sign-off.

blocks.heading: Users and Access
blocks.body: Profiles and permission sets decide what someone can do. Org-wide defaults, roles and sharing rules decide which records they see.

blocks.heading: Reports and Dashboards
blocks.body: Reports list and summarise records. Dashboards present reports visually. List views filter records on a tab.

blocks.heading: The Ecosystem
blocks.body: AppExchange for apps, Trailhead for learning, three seasonal releases a year, sandboxes for testing before production.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Associate
nextCertsAfter.intro: Good next steps after Platform Foundations:

sampleQuestions.question: Who is the Salesforce Associate certification designed for?
options: Individuals with up to 6 months of user experience on Salesforce
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Associate certification is designed for individuals who may have up to 6 months of user experience.
whyWrong: 'Developers only' is too narrow, this associate-level credential targets general users, not developers specifically.
'Architects only' is too narrow; this is an entry-level credential, not an architect-level one.
'Marketers only' is too narrow, this credential targets general platform users, not a specific role.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Customer 360 Platform refer to?
options: The integrated set of Salesforce products that connect customer data across the organization
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer 360 is Salesforce's integrated platform connecting customer data across products.
whyWrong: 'Only Marketing Cloud' undersells Customer 360, which spans the full integrated product suite.
'Only Service Cloud' undersells Customer 360, which spans the full integrated product suite.
'Only Sales Cloud' undersells Customer 360, which spans the full integrated product suite, not one cloud.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object is central to the Salesforce CRM data model?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account is a core object representing companies or people you do business with.
whyWrong: Dashboard visualizes data, it isn't the central CRM data model object.
Report is a data display tool, not the central data model object.
Email Template is a content asset, unrelated to the core data model.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Record in Salesforce?
options: A single row of data in an object (e.g., one Account)
sampleQuestions.explanation: A record is a single row of data in an object.
whyWrong: A dashboard visualizes data, it isn't itself a single row of data.
A permission set controls access, it isn't a data row.
A report type defines report structure, not an individual data row.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature allows users to see their tasks and calendar?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Home page and Activity components show tasks and calendar.
whyWrong: 'Only list views' misattributes the task/calendar visibility to a different feature.
'Only dashboards' misattributes the task/calendar visibility to a different feature.
'Reports only' undersells the Home page feature, which includes activity/calendar components too.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a Dashboard in Salesforce?
options: A collection of report components displayed together for at-a-glance visibility
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dashboards display multiple report charts and metrics in a single view.
whyWrong: A single report shows one dataset, a Dashboard combines multiple report components together.
An email template is a content asset, unrelated to Dashboards.
A list view shows a filtered record list, it isn't the multi-component visual summary a Dashboard provides.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce feature enables real-time collaboration on records?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Chatter and Activity enable comments, mentions, and collaboration on records.
whyWrong: Validation rules enforce data entry rules, they aren't a collaboration feature.
Workflow rules automate backend logic, they aren't a real-time collaboration feature.
'Reports only' misattributes real-time collaboration to a display feature, not a collaboration tool.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Lightning Experience refer to?
options: The modern Salesforce user interface with responsive design and enhanced features
sampleQuestions.explanation: Lightning Experience is the modern, responsive Salesforce UI.
whyWrong: 'Classic only' is the opposite of what Lightning Experience refers to; Classic is the older interface.
Lightning Experience isn't limited to mobile, it's the full desktop and mobile modern interface.
An API is a technical integration mechanism, not a user interface.

sampleQuestions.question: Which object typically represents a person or company you do business with?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Account represents companies or people you do business with.
whyWrong: Opportunity represents a potential sale, not the person/company relationship itself.
Task is an activity record, not the person/company relationship object.
Report is a data display tool, unrelated to representing a person or company.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a List View in Salesforce?
options: A filtered list of records from an object displayed in a table format
sampleQuestions.explanation: List views show filtered records in a tabular layout for quick access.
whyWrong: A report type defines report structure, it isn't itself the filtered record list being described.
A permission set controls access, it isn't a filtered list of records.
A dashboard visualizes data, it isn't the filtered table view being described.

sampleQuestions.question: Which navigation element helps users find records and apps in Salesforce?
sampleQuestions.explanation: App Launcher and global search help users navigate and find content.
whyWrong: Workflow automates backend logic, it's unrelated to navigation and search.
Validation rules enforce data quality, they're unrelated to navigation.
'Report Builder only' misattributes navigation/search to a different, unrelated reporting tool.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Customer 360 Platform aim to achieve?
options: A single, unified view of the customer across all touchpoints and systems
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer 360 unifies customer data across sales, service, marketing, and more.
whyWrong: 'Only service cloud' undersells Customer 360's broader unified cross-touchpoint vision.
'Only marketing' undersells Customer 360's broader unified cross-touchpoint vision.
'Only sales automation' undersells Customer 360's broader unified cross-touchpoint vision.

sampleQuestions.question: Which feature allows users to access Salesforce on mobile devices?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Salesforce Mobile App provides full CRM access on phones and tablets.
whyWrong: Reports alone don't provide the mobile access capability being described.
Email access doesn't provide the full mobile app experience being described.
'Desktop only' contradicts the fact that the Salesforce Mobile App specifically enables mobile access.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Reports in Salesforce?
options: To organize, filter, and display data from your Salesforce records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reports query and display data from your org's objects and records.
whyWrong: 'To send emails only' misattributes Reports' purpose, which is data organization/display, not messaging.
'To assign tasks' misattributes Reports' purpose to an unrelated task-management function.
'To create dashboards only' undersells Reports, which serve their own distinct purpose beyond feeding dashboards.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce concept represents a potential sale?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Opportunity represents a potential sale or deal being pursued.
whyWrong: Lead represents an unqualified prospect, not yet the specific potential-sale concept an Opportunity represents.
Account represents a company/organization, not a potential sale itself.
Contact represents a person, not a potential sale.
